content.overview: Article 98 requires that each House of Parliament shall have a separate secretarial staff. Parliament may by law regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to the secretarial staff of either House. Pending such law, the President may, after consultation with the Speaker of the House of the People or the Chairman of the Council of States, as the case may be, make rules regulating recruitment and conditions of service; such rules have effect subject to the provisions of any law made under this article.
content.glance: Each House has separate secretarial staff. Recruitment/conditions: Parliament by law; until then, Presidential rules after consulting Speaker/Chairman.
content.study:
Article 98 establishes institutional autonomy of each House’s secretariat. Parliament may legislate on recruitment and service conditions; interim rules are made by the President after consultation with the Speaker or Chairman.

Examination: separate secretariats; parliamentary law; interim Presidential rules with consultation.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Separate secretarial staff for each House.
2. Recruitment and conditions of service: Parliament by law.
3. Until law: President may make rules after consulting Speaker (LS) or Chairman (RS).

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 98 provide regarding the Secretariat of Parliament?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 98 requires each House of Parliament to have a separate secretarial staff. Parliament may by law regulate recruitment and conditions of service. Until such law is made, the President may, after consultation with the Speaker or the Chairman as the case may be, make rules regulating recruitment and conditions of service.

examTips: Separate secretariat per House; law by Parliament; interim Presidential rules after consultation.

keyTakeaways: Art 98: separate secretariats; parliamentary regulation of staff.
